Thanks for the summary, Jasmine. Quick read of ProcSys' redlines — below are recommended positions and language we can propose back. High-level: we should be willing to concede a narrow output-ownership carveout as long as we retain a non-exclusive right to use generated output and de-identified feedback for service improvement. We should resist absolute prohibitions on training unless compensated.

Recommended counter-points (for legal redline):
- Output/Customer Content: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and Customer Generated Output. Redwood is granted a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Customer Content and Customer Generated Output solely to provide the Service to Customer, to operate and maintain the Service, and to perform aggregated, de-identified quality improvements to the Service. Such license does not permit Redwood to sell or sublicense Customer Generated Output as a standalone product."

- Training / Feedback License: "Customer may opt-out of having raw Customer Content used to train models. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable license to use anonymized and aggregated telemetry and Feedback (as defined below) to improve model quality and Service performance, provided that such Feedback cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstitute Customer Content. 'Feedback' excludes any Customer Content marked as sensitive in the Order Form. Redwood shall maintain an auditable record of data used for model training and make such evidence available to Customer upon request for compliance purposes."

- Telemetry Definition & Controls: include an appendix that enumerates allowed telemetry fields (e.g., token usage counts, latency, anonymized prompt/response fingerprints, error traces) and excludes PII and verbatim prompts unless explicit opt-in is checked in the Order Form. Propose an "Opt-Out Toggle" on the account with a 30-day effectivity window.

Commercial proposal (recommended):
- Offer: if Customer opts into anonymized-telemetry training for a subset of workloads, reduce recurring unit price by 5% for the first 12 months (to account for training value). If Customer requires a hard ban on training on any derivative of their data, propose a one-time premium (e.g., 15% uplift) to offset lost model improvement value.

Operational notes for Karthik: if we accept an opt-out, we must ensure tooling to filter flagged datasets from training pipelines and preserve KV caches properly. This is doable but will require a scoped implementation ticket and ~4-6 weeks runbook work.

Next steps: I can draft exact redline snippets for each clause and run them by Legal Ops. Jasmine — confirm whether Marissa is ok to present the 5% concession or we prefer a different commercial offset.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
